pageProps.review: Learn how to install and configure NVM (Node Version Manager) and discover tips for easily installing and managing various versions of Node.js to build an optimized development environment for each project.
pageProps.content:
## Efficient Node.js Management using NVM (Node Version Manager)
Using <mark>NVM (Node Version Manager)</mark> makes it easy to switch between different Node.js versions for each project, making development environment configuration much more pleasant.
### Install NVM
Execute the NVM installation script by entering the command below in the terminal.  
You can check for the latest version and modify it as needed before installation.
```sh
{
    "title": "Install NVM"
}
---
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
# Or using wget
wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
```
### Configure Shell
After installation, the settings are added to your shell environment file (such as `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`).  
To apply the changes immediately, enter the following command.
```sh
{
    "title": "Apply configure in shell"
}
---
$ source ~/.zshrc  # Zsh
# or
$ source ~/.bash_profile # Bash
```
### Install Node.js
If <mark>NVM</mark> is installed correctly, you can now install the desired version of Node.js.  
I recommend installing the `latest LTS` version.
```sh
{
    "title": "Install Node.js"
}
---
$ nvm install --lts
```
Specific versions can also be installed.
```sh
{
    "title": "Install specific version of Node.js"
}
---
$ nvm install 18.17.0
```
### Manage Versions
You can check installed versions or switch between them freely.
| Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `nvm ls` | Check all installed Node versions |
| `nvm use <version>` | Switch to a specific version |
| `nvm alias default <version>` | Set default version when terminal starts |
